telemetry.implementation: Each standalone service retains a self-contained bootstrap because infrastructure build contexts cannot safely depend on an unpublished shared runtime package. CI enforces one behavioral and dependency contract across those bootstraps.

reliability.objectiveStatus: Operator starting points, not claims about an undeployed environment. Every production deployment must adopt them or record a measured, reviewed override.
reliability.availability: Start at 99.9% successful readiness-eligible protocol requests per rolling 30 days, excluding approved maintenance.
reliability.errors: Page when server-side failures or failed critical journeys consume 10% of the monthly error budget in one hour or 5% in six hours.
reliability.latency: Define route- and payload-class p95/p99 objectives from production baselines; never combine small JSON calls with uploads, downloads, sync, or batch traffic.
dashboardPanels: request rate, status class, and duration by route and payload class
event-loop delay, heap, garbage collection, CPU, and memory
database pool saturation, query latency, and migration state
rate-limit, concurrency-limit, timeout, and body-limit rejections
trace-linked structured errors by operation and deployment version
backup age, restore-test age, replica health, and storage capacity

incidentResponse: Detect from readiness, error-budget, latency, saturation, security, and backup alerts.
Triage with deployment version, correlated trace and log fields, dependency health, and recent migration evidence.
Contain by stopping rollout, removing readiness, restricting administrative paths, or reverting only when persistence compatibility is known.
Recover from a verified image and backup or reproducible source; never improvise schema rollback on live state.
Verify protocol critical journeys, dependency health, telemetry delivery, and data integrity before resolving.
Record impact, timeline, cause, corrective actions, evidence, and tracker follow-ups without secrets.

deployment.productionDisruptionPolicy: Stateful or singleton-safe services require an explicit maintenance strategy; horizontally safe services require a PodDisruptionBudget that preserves at least one ready replica.
deployment.productionTopologyPolicy: Spread ready replicas across failure domains where the service's shared state and session model support horizontal operation.
deployment.productionAutoscalingPolicy: Scale only from measured saturation and latency signals, with bounded minimum and maximum replicas and a verified shared-state/session design.
deployment.runtimeContract: Hosted Linux/amd64 CI builds every governed image and requires non-root and health metadata, closed invalid-configuration behavior, successful startup, liveness, readiness after any startup-owned migration, credential-free wildcard CORS, one minimal public protocol transaction, and clean SIGTERM shutdown. Disposable MySQL, MongoDB, and source-built Wallet Infrastructure dependencies are used where the real service requires them; no image is pushed.

services.name: chaintracks-server
criticalJourneys: return current chain information
serve a bounded bulk-header object
ingest and persist a verified header
alerts: header tip age or height stops advancing
bulk-header export or upstream retrieval repeatedly fails
API or CDN saturation exceeds its independent concurrency budget
services.state: Bulk-header files under BULK_HEADERS_PATH; upstream headers are reproducible.
services.migration: No schema migration. Validate the retained header corpus before rollout.
services.backup: Snapshot BULK_HEADERS_PATH or repopulate it from a verified source CDN.
services.rpo: 24 hours when reproducible upstreams are healthy; otherwise match the operator's header-retention risk.
services.rto: 4 hours from a verified snapshot or reproducible upstream.
services.restoreValidation: Verify header-chain continuity, tip agreement, bulk-object hashes, and both HTTP listeners.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT stop ingestion and export timers, drain API and CDN listeners, destroy Chaintracks state, and flush telemetry.
lifecycle.scaling: Prefer one ingest leader; CDN readers may scale only against shared immutable storage.
lifecycle.disruption: Preserve the ingest leader or use an explicit handoff during voluntary disruption.
lifecycle.topology: Separate replicated CDN readers from the ingest leader when availability requires it.

services.name: message-box-server
criticalJourneys: authenticate a peer and list messages
persist and deliver a message once
acknowledge a delivered message
establish and use an authenticated WebSocket
alerts: message persistence succeeds but delivery or acknowledgement repeatedly fails
authenticated WebSocket handshakes or delivery failures spike
wallet storage, database, or Firebase dependency failures consume error budget
services.state: Knex database plus optional Firebase device registrations.
services.migration: Migrations complete before listen; back up and verify the target schema first.
services.backup: Use the selected database engine's consistent snapshot and restore procedure.
services.rpo: 15 minutes for messages and permissions; device registrations follow the same backup boundary when enabled.
services.rto: 4 hours from a verified database backup and wallet configuration.
services.restoreValidation: Verify migration state, authenticated list/send/acknowledge, duplicate handling, and optional push delivery.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT disconnect authenticated WebSockets, drain HTTP, close Knex, and flush telemetry. The standalone compatibility adapter uses only the published AuthSocket public socket surface and automatically delegates to AuthSocketServer.close() when that API is available.
lifecycle.scaling: Multiple replicas require shared BRC-103 sessions, database-backed rate limits, and a verified WebSocket routing strategy.
lifecycle.disruption: Preserve at least one ready replica only after shared session and WebSocket behavior is proven.
lifecycle.topology: Spread replicas after shared-state requirements are met; otherwise operate as an explicit singleton.

services.name: overlay-server
criticalJourneys: submit and propagate a transaction without creating local-only state
query each enabled lookup service
ingest and classify provider callbacks
reconcile GASP/BASM state across a reorganization
alerts: readiness dependency checks fail or provider callback processing errors repeat
unproven rows age beyond policy or maintenance repeatedly fails
BASM tip, reorg stream, or GASP synchronization becomes stale
services.state: Knex transaction state and MongoDB lookup-service state.
services.migration: Overlay migrations complete before listen; preserve both stores as one release boundary.
services.backup: Take coordinated MySQL and MongoDB backups before schema or image changes.
services.rpo: 15 minutes across a coordinated SQL and MongoDB backup boundary.
services.rto: 4 hours from mutually consistent backups and verified provider configuration.
services.restoreValidation: Verify schema versions, topic and lookup counts, submit/lookup, provider callbacks, GASP/BASM anchors, and readiness.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT idempotently stop synchronization and maintenance work, drain HTTP, close Knex and MongoDB, and flush telemetry. The standalone compatibility adapter delegates to OverlayExpress.close() when available without requiring an unpublished dependency.
lifecycle.scaling: Background GASP/BASM/maintenance ownership and BRC-103 sessions must be coordinated before adding replicas.
lifecycle.disruption: Operate as a singleton unless leader election and shared sessions are proven; record a maintenance window for voluntary disruption.
lifecycle.topology: After coordination is implemented, spread ready replicas and database replicas across independent failure domains.

services.name: uhrp-server-basic
criticalJourneys: quote and authenticate an upload
persist and retrieve content without hash drift
renew retained content
alerts: content write, hash verification, retrieval, or renewal failures repeat
filesystem capacity or inode headroom crosses operator thresholds
wallet storage authentication or payment failures consume error budget
services.state: Local files and metadata under the configured public storage directory.
services.migration: No schema migration; preserve file and metadata consistency.
services.backup: Snapshot the complete storage directory and verify hashes before restore.
services.rpo: 1 hour or the accepted paid-content durability window, whichever is stricter.
services.rto: 4 hours from a verified filesystem snapshot and wallet configuration.
services.restoreValidation: Verify a sample of content hashes and metadata, upload/download/renew, wallet authentication, and capacity.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT remove readiness, drain HTTP, destroy the cached wallet client, and flush telemetry.
lifecycle.scaling: Use one writer unless content and metadata live on a concurrency-safe shared filesystem and rate limits are shared.
lifecycle.disruption: Protect the writer or schedule a maintenance window; never overlap independent local filesystems behind one hostname.
lifecycle.topology: Replicate only with a storage design that preserves hash-addressed consistency.

services.name: uhrp-server-cloud-bucket
criticalJourneys: quote and authenticate a cloud upload
persist and retrieve an object without hash drift
renew retained content
alerts: bucket authorization, write, read, metadata, or retention failures repeat
provider quota, throttling, versioning, or replication health degrades
wallet storage authentication or payment failures consume error budget
services.state: Cloud bucket objects and provider metadata.
services.migration: No local schema migration; validate provider configuration before listen.
services.backup: Use provider versioning/replication and verify object hashes and retention policy.
services.rpo: 1 hour or the configured provider replication objective, whichever is stricter.
services.rto: 4 hours from provider replicas/versioning and verified wallet configuration.
services.restoreValidation: Verify object hashes, metadata, retention, upload/download/renew, and provider IAM boundaries.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT remove readiness, drain HTTP, destroy the cached wallet client, and flush telemetry.
lifecycle.scaling: Multiple replicas require shared rate limits and a cloud provider configuration safe for concurrent writers.
lifecycle.disruption: Preserve at least one ready replica after shared rate-limit behavior is verified.
lifecycle.topology: Spread replicas independently from the bucket's own regional durability boundary.

services.name: wab
criticalJourneys: start and complete an authentication challenge
store, retrieve, update, and delete encrypted shares
link, unlink, and delete an identity safely
alerts: SMS challenge, completion, replay, or abuse-control failures spike
share encryption, retrieval, or deletion failures repeat
database migration or pool failures consume error budget
services.state: Authentication, identity-link, share, deletion-intent, and faucet database tables.
services.migration: Migrations complete before listen; verify rollback compatibility before rollout.
services.backup: Take an encrypted database snapshot and test identity/share recovery without logging secrets.
services.rpo: 15 minutes for authentication and encrypted share state.
services.rto: 4 hours from a verified encrypted backup and independently retained encryption keys.
services.restoreValidation: Verify migration state, authentication completion, share round-trip, identity links, deletion, rate limits, and audit-safe logs.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT drain HTTP, close Knex, and flush telemetry.
lifecycle.scaling: Multiple replicas require shared rate limits and any authentication challenge/session state to remain database-backed.
lifecycle.disruption: Preserve at least one ready replica after shared abuse-control state is verified.
lifecycle.topology: Spread ready replicas and use a highly available managed or operator-owned database.

services.name: wallet-infra
criticalJourneys: authenticate and execute representative storage RPC
create and retrieve wallet state without schema drift
run monitor tasks and advance proof state
alerts: storage RPC errors, authorization failures, or latency consume error budget
monitor tasks stop, fail repeatedly, or proof state stops advancing
database migration, pool saturation, or storage-capacity health degrades
services.state: Wallet Storage database, monitor state, transactions, outputs, baskets, and certificates.
services.migration: Storage migration and availability checks complete before the server starts.
services.backup: Take and verify a consistent database backup before every schema or image change.
services.rto: 4 hours from a verified backup, identity key, and service-provider configuration.
services.restoreValidation: Verify schema and storage identity, authenticated RPC, representative wallet state, monitor progress, and provider connectivity.

lifecycle.shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT stop monitor tasks, terminate optional nginx, drain StorageServer, destroy wallet storage, and flush telemetry.
lifecycle.scaling: Operate one monitor leader; API replicas require shared sessions, rate limits, storage, and explicit monitor leadership.
lifecycle.disruption: Protect the monitor leader or perform an explicit handoff; preserve ready API capacity only after shared-state behavior is proven.
lifecycle.topology: Separate monitor leadership from horizontally safe API capacity when production demand justifies it.
